Hi Ella — thanks for the questionnaire, attaching a concise set of answers and a one-pager for your InfoSec review. High-level responses below; see attachments for the retention table and sample audit log. Happy to join a call if you want to walk through.

1) Storage & region pinning
- Hosted API: customers may pin their tenant to a geographic region (US, EU, or APAC). Default is US (region selection at signup).
- Storage is provisioned in the chosen cloud region and we do not move customer content outside the chosen geography for normal operation.
- For DR we replicate metadata into a secondary zone within the same geography; no cross-geography replicas for pinned tenants unless explicitly requested and contractually approved.

2) Retention windows
- Request payloads (primary request/response bodies): default 30 days for operational monitoring and abuse detection; configurable by enterprise contract.
- API request logs / telemetry: retained 90 days for troubleshooting and security investigations; aggregate metrics stored longer for product analytics.
- Backups/snapshots: infrastructure snapshots for operational recovery are retained up to 90 days; these snapshots do not contain long-term customer content caches (see backups paragraph).

3) Backups and emergency artifacts
- We do not bake full customer request stores into long-lived backups. Backups primarily cover infra state and model binaries.
- In rare debugging scenarios we may capture a short-lived crash dump that contains customer request context; these are time-limited and explicitly flagged. By default, these artifacts are retained only for the troubleshooting window (up to 30 days) and are deleted after resolution.

4) Deletion / erasure process
- Customer-initiated deletion: we provide an API and portal request flow. Typical purge timeline: primary data stores and indexes cleared within 72 hours of a confirmed request, in-memory caches evicted within minutes, search indexes and auxiliary caches removed within 24 hours, and full confirmation completed within 7 days.
- For backups and DR snapshots that may conceptually include emergency artifacts, we mark and remove any captured customer content following a documented deletion workflow; full removal from backups completes within the 90-day backup retention window unless a separate remediation process is used (we can provide an accelerated plan under contract).

5) Model training & data use
- By default, customer request content is not used to train or improve models. We offer an explicit opt-in program for customers who want to contribute telemetry for model improvements; opt-in is documented in contracts and governed by data processing addenda.

6) Compliance evidence
- SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 in progress, GDPR-ready controls and DPA. Sample audit log attached (redacted, synthetic identifiers).

Hi Ella — following internal confirmation, a succinct set of final answers (suitable for Legal/InfoSec). I’ve attached the redacted audit sample and a revised one-pager with exact policy language. Please find the confirmed points below.

1) Backups & cross-region replication
- Backups and infra snapshots are stored within the customer’s chosen geography by default. For high-availability DR we replicate metadata and infra state to a secondary zone within the same geography.
- We do not replicate customer content or emergency artifacts to a different geography unless explicitly requested and contractually approved (we will provide a documented risk assessment for cross-geography replication requests).

2) Ephemeral caches and KV stores
- Streaming KV caches used to accelerate token generation are in-memory or short-lived local caches and are evicted within minutes of session end. Ephemeral caches are not included in long-lived backups and are removed within 24 hours in normal operation.
- The 30-day default retention window applies to persisted request payloads kept for operational monitoring and abuse review; it does not extend the lifetime of ephemeral in-memory caches.

3) Metadata usage (IP, headers, tenant id)
- Request metadata is retained for security and operational troubleshooting and is part of our 90-day log retention. We do not use tenant-level request metadata for model training or external analytics products by default. Any use of metadata for analytics or product telemetry is aggregated and pseudonymized; export of raw metadata to third-party analytics occurs only under customer-approved configurations.

4) Deletion / erasure SLA
- Confirmed purge timeline: primary data stores and indexes cleared within 72 hours; caches evicted within minutes; search indexes and auxiliary caches removed within 24 hours; final confirmation within 7 days. If customer requests accelerated removal from backups, we will coordinate a remediation plan (contract amendment required) — standard backup retention remains 90 days.

5) Model training opt-in
- By default, customer request content and metadata are not used to train models. Model improvement pipelines only consume customer data following an explicit, documented opt-in and written consent in the DPA.

Attachments included: audit_log_sample.txt (redacted sample), DataResidency_OnePager.pdf (policy language)

Customer request content is not used for model training unless the customer has explicitly opted in. Deletion requests are processed with primary purge completed within 72 hours and final confirmation within 7 days.”
